purpose: Ergonomic SQLite bindings; provides the bundled-sqlcipher-vendored-openssl feature that gives us encryption at rest
maintenance: Actively maintained; frequent releases tracking upstream SQLite
security_implications: Parses untrusted-derived values but not untrusted file formats. SQL is always parameterised; no string-built queries outside the SQLCipher PRAGMA key path (which cannot be bound and is escaped by doubling quotes).
replacement_strategy: libsql-rusqlite is an API-compatible fork; the store layer is behind kokin-store so callers never see rusqlite types

purpose: Derive macro for error enums; keeps the wrong-passphrase vs corruption distinction expressible without hand-written Display impls
maintenance: Actively maintained by dtolnay; de-facto standard
security_implications: None at runtime — proc macro expands to plain impls
replacement_strategy: Hand-written Display/Error impls; mechanical to remove

purpose: Transitive: builds OpenSSL from source for SQLCipher's crypto
security_implications: Large C attack surface, but only the crypto primitives are reached — no TLS stack is used by the storage layer. Security updates require a dependency bump and a release.
replacement_strategy: Switch to bundled-sqlcipher against a system OpenSSL, or re-open ADR-0004

purpose: Desktop shell using the OS webview; provides window management, IPC, and the permission system
security_implications: The webview renders our own bundled assets only, under a strict CSP. Untrusted collected HTML is never rendered here — it goes through sanitisation into a sandboxed iframe.
replacement_strategy: Electron (rejected, ADR-0001) — would require rewriting the shell layer only, not the kokin-* crates

security_implications: Deserialises IPC input from our own frontend. Typed structs, no arbitrary-type deserialisation.
replacement_strategy: No practical alternative; universal in the Rust ecosystem

purpose: UI framework; compiles away rather than shipping a runtime, keeping the bundle small and large evidence tables fast
security_implications: Renders application-controlled data. Collected content is escaped by default; dangerous HTML injection points are forbidden by review and CI.
replacement_strategy: React or Vue; would require rewriting the UI layer only

purpose: Frontend build tool and dev server
security_implications: Build-time only. Supply-chain risk is managed by npm ci against a committed lockfile.

purpose: Argon2id password-based key derivation; turns a user passphrase into the key-encrypting key
maintenance: RustCrypto project; widely used and audited-adjacent. Steady release cadence.
approx_size: <200KB compiled; runtime memory cost is the tuned 64MiB per derivation
security_implications: Processes the user's own passphrase, not attacker-controlled input. Parameters are pinned in a versioned profile so a defaults change cannot silently strand existing cases. Verified byte-identical to the reference C implementation via a known-answer test.
replacement_strategy: Any RFC 9106 Argon2id implementation; the KAT makes a swap verifiable rather than a leap of faith

purpose: XChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD used to wrap the case master key under the KEK and the recovery key
security_implications: The 192-bit extended nonce means random nonces need no counter state, removing a whole class of nonce-reuse bugs. AEAD binds ciphertext to the case id and KDF profile via AAD, so a wrapped key cannot be transplanted between cases.
replacement_strategy: aes-gcm from the same project; would require re-wrapping existing keys, so treat as a format migration

purpose: Clears key material from memory on drop; derive feature provides ZeroizeOnDrop
maintenance: RustCrypto project; stable and slow-moving by design
security_implications: Reduces how long keys linger in memory. Does not defend against a live-process memory read, and the module documents that rather than implying otherwise.
replacement_strategy: Hand-written Drop impls using volatile writes; error-prone, which is why the crate exists

purpose: Constant-time equality for secrets, so key comparison does not leak via timing
security_implications: Prevents the derived PartialEq short-circuit from revealing how many leading bytes of a guessed key were correct.
replacement_strategy: No good alternative; hand-rolled constant-time code is routinely optimised away by the compiler

purpose: OS CSPRNG for master keys, recovery keys, salts, and nonces
maintenance: Actively maintained; the ecosystem's standard entropy source
security_implications: Reads directly from the OS entropy source (BCryptGenRandom on Windows, getentropy on macOS). Chosen over rand_core to avoid the RNG trait churn across rand 0.6/0.9/0.10 and to keep the entropy path short and auditable.

purpose: JSON for Tauri IPC payloads and for the plaintext case header (header.json)
security_implications: Parses the case header, which is attacker-writable if someone has filesystem access. Malformed input is handled as a named MalformedHeader error rather than a panic, and the wrapped keys inside are AEAD-authenticated so a tampered header fails to unwrap rather than yielding a wrong key. Missing from this registry until 2026-08-12 despite being in use since increment 1.
replacement_strategy: Any serde-compatible format; the header format version field exists so a format change is a migration rather than a break

purpose: Hash for the audit chain and, later, content-addressed blobs
maintenance: Actively maintained by the authors of the BLAKE3 spec
security_implications: Fast and tree-structured, which matters for hashing large evidence blobs later. Not a password hash and never used as one - that is Argon2id's job in kokin-keys. No untrusted input parsing.
replacement_strategy: SHA-256 via sha2; would change every stored hash, so it is a format migration not a swap

purpose: Deterministic CBOR encoding of audit payloads before hashing
maintenance: Maintained under the enarx project; stable and low-churn
security_implications: Encodes our own structured data for hashing; does not decode untrusted input on this path. Chosen over JSON because JSON guarantees nothing about key order or number formatting, so two equivalent encodings would hash differently and break the chain for no real reason.
replacement_strategy: Any canonical CBOR implementation; the hash input format would need a version bump

purpose: WHATWG-compliant URL parsing for canonical_locator, raw_locator, and fixture replay keys
maintenance: Maintained by the servo project; the de-facto standard and very widely depended on
security_implications: Parses attacker-influenced URLs, which is exactly why it is a dependency rather than hand-rolled: URL parsing is a well-known source of allowlist-bypass bugs (userinfo tricks, mixed encodings, IDN homographs) and a hand-written parser would be a security defect generator. Also supplies form_urlencoded for canonical query serialisation.
replacement_strategy: No serious alternative in Rust; a hand-rolled parser is the option this dependency exists to avoid
